_about: Leica Q3 settings-file codes: what each is thought to be and how sure. Firmware 4.1, 587 codes: the 586 in Hudson Henry's 4.1.1 Q3 file plus D17A, which every other Q3 file has. Built 2026-11-17 from a first pass and three focused passes checked against the public USB tests, then merged the same day with: settings files from Ken Rockwell (Q3, 4.1.0), Florian Froschmayer (Q3 and Q3 43, 3.1; SL3 4.2.0 and SL3-S 3.1.1; with labeled button PDFs), four exports from three Leica forum members (Q3, 2024); menu screens in seven videos by three presenters, read against the presenters' own files; Leica maker notes in Q3 photos; release notes dated against the files; Nick Rains' and Jono Slack's labeled SL3 files. Known 95, likely 218, guess 169, unknown 105. Known needs two independent sources, or one match of the camera's own screen, or the photographer's own words, to their own file on a value changed from factory. Fields: first_seen is the first firmware whose files hold the code (1-2: 326, 3.0: 6, 3.1: 231, 4: 24); new_in_fw4 is first_seen 4 (24 codes); factory is the value in Ken Rockwell's never-saved profiles 3 and 4 (firmware 4.1.0), with factory_note where his four never-saved profiles disagree. _retired lists the 18 codes older files have and 4.1 files do not; _generations the code sets by firmware. The Q3 and the SL3 run one software platform (their open-source packages are identical) and share 510 codes on firmware 4. Nothing here has been tested by importing a file on a Q3.

3.name: Magnification
3.evidence: SL3 table 'Magnification'; M list 'Focus Aid' (the M's magnifier). Factory video Center button in the old Q3 file. Froschmayer's SL3 PDF labels the front upper button Magnification; his SL3 4.2.0 file holds 3 there.

4.name: Drive Mode
4.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; first item of Hudson's photo list; sits in the Control Center slot the manual shows as Drive Mode. Froschmayer's SL3 PDF: Drive Mode on the top button, file 4.

5.name: Self-timer
5.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; follows Bracketing in Hudson's photo list, as in the manual's menu order. A forum member's 'TIME LASPE' profile (2024) puts 5 on the thumbwheel button.

6.name: Interval Shooting
6.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; follows Drive Mode in Hudson's photo list.

7.name: Exposure Bracketing
7.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; follows Interval Shooting in Hudson's photo list.

8.name: Capture Assistants
8.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; last item of both Q3 43 lists. The SL3 editor's table and the Q3's own full button lists (2024 forum files, in menu order) agree on it.

9.name: Exposure Metering
9.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; follows the focus items in both of Hudson's lists.

10.name: Exposure Compensation
10.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; Hudson's video thumbwheel button.

11.name: ISO (the Q3 menu calls it ISO Settings)
11.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; Q3 factory thumbwheel button is 11 in the old file and 'ISO Settings' in the manual (p. 40 and p. 228). The camera's own label 'ISO' in photo metadata (maker-note tag 0x042D) for the factory thumbwheel button and for Ken Rockwell's FN 2. Nick Rains' SL3 PDF changes a button from WB to ISO and his file goes from 15 to 11; Froschmayer's SL3 PDF: ISO, file 11.

12.name: Auto ISO Settings
12.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; Q3 43 FN 2 switches between 11 and 12 per profile.

15.name: White Balance
15.evidence: M firmware button list and SL3 editor table agree; between Auto ISO and Gray Card in Hudson's video list. Nick Rains' SL3 PDF: top-right button 'WB', file 15 in his untouched slots; Froschmayer's SL3 PDF: White Balance on the video top button, file 15.

16.name: Gray Card
16.evidence: SL3 table (the M uses 17); directly after White Balance in Hudson's video list.

The camera's own label 'Digital Zoom' for FN 1 in photo metadata (maker-note tag 0x042D). Froschmayer's Q3 PDF: video FN 1 Digital Zoom, file 21.

The Q3's own full button lists (2024 forum files) place 22 between JPG resolution (94?) and iDR (56), where Film Style is in the menu; the M and SL3 tables also give 22 = Film Style.

30.name: Delete Single (review mode)
30.evidence: Manual p. 127 and p. 231 both give FN 1 in review = Delete Single; D190 (FN 1 review on the M) is 30 in every Q3 file. Also appears in both Q3 43 custom lists, which does not fit a review function: open.

32.name: Delete Unrated? (M: 'Delete All without star')

44.name: Focus Mode

Froschmayer's Q3 PDF labels FN 1 Toggle Focus Point and his Q3 file holds 82; his SL3 PDF and file agree. The Q3 3.1.1 release notes made Toggle Focus Point assignable to a function button. The SL3 editor's table: 82.

85.name: Clipping

88.name: Perspective Control
88.evidence: Both of Hudson's bodies, every profile. Not in the M or SL3 tables. Candidates by menu: AF-L / AE-L / AF-L + AE-L, Thumbwheel, AF Frame Size, Toggle Focus Point. Hudson Henry's thumbwheel-button popup opens on Perspective Control and he says so (firmware 4.0 video, December 2025); both his files (October 2026) hold 88 there. List order and the SL3 editor's table put Perspective Control at 110; the camera's screen wins and 110 stays open. He may have changed the button between video and file. Test: set the thumbwheel button to Perspective Control and export. A 2024 forum export uses 88 on FN 2.

92.name: unknown focus item
92.evidence: After 46 and before Exposure Metering in both of Hudson's lists, so a Focusing item offered in photo and video (Touch AF, Touch AF in EVF, AF Frame Size are candidates).

94.name: Max. JPG Resolution?
94.evidence: Between DNG Resolution (19) and Film Style (22) in the Q3's own lists, the place of Max. JPG-Resolution in the 2023 Wi-Fi menu; the SL3 uses 49 for its JPG resolution. A forum member puts 94 on the Center and thumbwheel buttons.

104.name: AF-L + AE-L
104.evidence: 104, 105, 106 are between Digital Zoom (21) and Magnification (3) in every full Q3 list, where the firmware 4 manual's direct-access table has Exposure lock: AF-L + AE-L, AE-L, AF-L.

105.name: AE-L
105.evidence: Second of the exposure-lock trio, see 104.

106.name: AF-L
106.evidence: Hudson's photo FN 1 on both bodies; in the Q3 43 video list directly after Gray Card (16), where Color Temperature sits in the menu. SL3 table has Color temperature at 108. Hudson Henry's FN 1 popup opens on AF-L and he describes it as the autofocus lock; his FN 1 holds 106 on both bodies (factory 21). Separately, list order puts AF-L third in the exposure-lock trio 104, 105, 106. Replaces the Color Temperature guess (that is 108).

107.name: Magnification in video? (the SL3 editor's table: Auto Magnification)
107.evidence: Froschmayer's SL3 PDF labels the front upper button Magnification on the video page; his SL3 4.2.0 file holds 107 there (older SL3 files hold 146). The SL3 editor's table calls 107 Auto magnification, and the Q3's lists put it after Focus Aid (46). Both readings are open.

108.name: Color Temperature
108.evidence: The SL3 editor's table and the Q3's own full button lists (2024 forum files, in menu order) agree on it; it follows Gray Card (16) in every Q3 list, as in the manual.

110.name: Perspective Control on the SL3 (the editor's table); unresolved on the Q3
110.evidence: List order and the SL3 editor's table give Perspective Control, but Hudson Henry's screen gives Perspective Control for 88. Unresolved.

111.name: Microphone Gain
111.evidence: The SL3 editor's table and the Q3's own full button lists (2024 forum files, in menu order) agree on it; only in the Q3 43 video list.

115.name: Video Profiles
115.evidence: Video Control Center slot 6; manual p. 24 and p. 45 show Video Profiles there.

120.name: Camera Settings (menu page)
120.evidence: Photo Control Center slot 1; manual shows the exposure mode tile there and lists Scene Mode first. Hudson Henry replaced the factory Scene Mode tile with Camera Settings in all his profiles and opens it on screen; D31B = 120. The earlier entry read 120 as Scene Mode; the factory tile is 158.

124.name: unknown
124.evidence: Q3 43 only, in D36C and D36E.

131.name: Leica Looks
131.evidence: Control Center slot 8 in both modes; manual shows Leica Looks there for photo and video.

158.evidence: Video Control Center slot 1; manual shows the exposure mode tile there. Factory D31B and D31C are both 158 (Ken Rockwell's never-saved profiles); Hudson Henry calls the tile he replaced 'scene mode'.

D054.evidence: Ordered, zero-terminated list of function numbers (same numbering as the buttons). Hudson fills items 1-11 (4,6,7,5,43,44,45,46,92,9,10), Q3 43 items 1-5 (43,16,30,32,8); all 0 in the old file and on the SL3. Item 11 lands in D070 while D05E stays 0, so D05E-D06C are not list slots. First read as the per-mode On/Off list behind 'Customize Control > FN Buttons' (manual p. 54): Hudson's entries are all button-assignable and include Interval and Bracketing, which the Control Center cannot hold. Favorites is the alternative reading. The FN button custom lists are D1FA and D1FB, so this list is probably something else, most likely Favorites: items can be setting codes as well as job numbers (a 2024 forum export holds 53318 = 0xD046, image stabilization, in this list), as in the M's Favorites (D1A9), whose items are codes of other settings or menu numbers.

DA01.evidence: 16-byte record as 32 hex digits, same in all 7 profile slots of Hudson's files. First word = Look ID in the same numbering as D69C/D69D. 11 slots = 5 pre-installed Core Looks + 6 slots for downloaded Looks (the 2023 Wi-Fi menu list had exactly six 'Leica Look 1-6' slots). Q3 holds 15, 12, 13, 16, 11, 21; Q3 43 holds 15, 12, 13, 16, 11 and an empty slot 6. Odd and even codes are identical twins; odd = photo, even = video (see below). Byte 4 = 100 in every slot including empty ones, so it is a default, probably Intensity (manual: 'Intensity can be set as a percentage'). The five 1-nibbles never vary in Hudson's files. Records differ between profile slots: Ken Rockwell set Vivid with +2 Saturation and +2 Sharpening (guide, firmware 4.1.0), and only DA03 (photo, Vivid) changes, only in his two saved profiles and the live slot, from 0000000C6411111... to 0000000C6411122...; DA04 (video, Vivid) stays at the default. His photos show both changes (maker-note tag 0x0406). So odd codes are photo and even codes video, and digits 13 and 14 are Sharpness and Saturation in the manual's order (which is which cannot be told from this file). Look IDs: see D69C. The 3.1 files already hold an intensity per Look, about seven months before firmware 4.0.0 announced the Intensity control.
